topic: Polymorphism and Dynamic Binding with Virtual Functions
explanation: Polymorphism, meaning "many forms", allows you to treat objects of different classes in a uniform way.  This is crucial for building flexible and extensible code.  In C++, dynamic binding (runtime polymorphism) is achieved using virtual functions.  A virtual function is declared using the `virtual` keyword in the base class. When a virtual function is called through a pointer or reference to a base class, the correct version of the function (the one defined in the derived class) is executed at runtime. This enables you to write code that can work with objects of various derived classes without needing to know their specific types at compile time.  A common pitfall is forgetting the `virtual` keyword in the base class, leading to static binding (the base class function is always called).
keywords: C++ virtual functions, runtime polymorphism, dynamic binding, virtual keyword
